glossary.IELTS: IELTS is an English test (bands 0–9). Most master's courses ask for 6.5 overall, with no band under 6.
glossary.TOEFL: TOEFL iBT is an English test scored out of 120. Many universities ask for 90–100.
glossary.PTE: PTE Academic is a computer-based English test scored 10–90, with results in about 2 days.
glossary.Duolingo: The Duolingo English Test is a cheap online test scored 10–160; check that your university accepts it.
glossary.GRE: The GRE is a graduate entrance test used mainly by US universities for master's and PhD programmes.
glossary.GMAT: The GMAT is the business-school entrance test, used for MBA and many management master's.
glossary.SAT: The SAT is a US undergraduate entrance test; many universities are now test-optional.
glossary.SOP: A Statement of Purpose explains why you chose this course and how it fits your goals. Make it specific to each university.
glossary.LOR: A Letter of Recommendation comes from a teacher or manager who knows your work. Most courses want 2–3.
glossary.CAS: A CAS is the UK university's confirmation number you need before applying for the Student visa.
glossary.I-20: The I-20 is the form a US university issues so you can apply for the F-1 visa.
glossary.F-1: The F-1 is the US student visa. You'll pay the SEVIS fee and attend an interview at the US embassy.
glossary.OPT: OPT lets F-1 students work in the US for 12 months after graduating, related to their field of study.
glossary.STEM OPT: STEM OPT extends US work rights by 24 months for graduates of eligible STEM degrees.
glossary.PGWP: The Post-Graduation Work Permit lets graduates of eligible Canadian programmes work for up to 3 years.
glossary.GIC: A GIC is a deposit that shows Canada you can cover living costs; it's paid back to you in instalments.
glossary.SDS: Student Direct Stream was Canada's faster visa route; check the official site for its current status.
glossary.APS: The APS certificate verifies Indian academic documents and is required for German university and visa applications.
glossary.blocked account: A German blocked account holds a year of living costs; you can withdraw a fixed amount each month.
glossary.Graduate Route: The UK Graduate Route lets you stay and work for 2 years after your degree (3 for a PhD).
glossary.subclass 500: Subclass 500 is Australia's student visa. You'll need a CoE from your university and health insurance (OSHC).
glossary.OSHC: OSHC is the health insurance international students must hold for their whole stay in Australia.
glossary.CoE: A Confirmation of Enrolment is what an Australian university issues after you accept your offer and pay the deposit.
glossary.Stamp 1G: Stamp 1G lets graduates stay in Ireland to look for work after their degree.
glossary.ECTS: ECTS credits measure study load in Europe. One academic year is 60 ECTS.
glossary.GPA: GPA is the grade average many universities use. Convert your Indian marks with our grade converter.
glossary.CGPA: CGPA is your cumulative grade point average across all semesters.
glossary.SGPA: SGPA is your grade point average for a single semester.
glossary.NMC: The National Medical Commission sets the rules for Indians studying MBBS abroad to practise in India.
glossary.FMGE: FMGE is the screening test Indian graduates of foreign medical schools must pass to practise in India.
glossary.MBBS: MBBS is the medical degree. Abroad, check NMC rules on course length, language and internship.
glossary.Russell Group: The Russell Group is 24 research-intensive UK universities, such as Oxford, UCL and Manchester.
glossary.Ivy League: The Ivy League is 8 private US universities known for selectivity, such as Harvard and Yale.
glossary.intake: An intake is when a course starts. Popular ones are September/autumn and January/spring.
glossary.tuition: Tuition is what the university charges for teaching. It doesn't include rent, food or travel.
glossary.scholarship: Scholarships are gifts, not loans. Merit awards need strong grades; apply early because funds run out.
glossary.ROI: ROI (return on investment) compares what a degree costs with the salary it may lead to.
glossary.PR: PR means permanent residence: the right to live and work in a country without a time limit.
glossary.visa: A student visa lets you study in the country. You usually need an offer, proof of funds and health insurance.
